headline: Highest risk is data leakage from A's broad network egress into B's support workflow; other pairwise risks are limited by B's disabled I/O and no shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Agent A has no filesystem or MCP surface, and agent B has clipboard, stdin/stdout, and file I/O all disabled, so there is no plausible default injection bridge between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies A's text into B's prompt or clipboard, injection becomes possible.
IF B is reconfigured to read files or stdin/stdout, A-authored content could become an instruction channel.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or message queues.
Do not pipe A's outputs directly into B's prompt.
Enable provenance tags on any handoff text.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer that strips instruction-like markup before B consumes A output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A advertises broad network egress, while B has no file, clipboard, or stdin/stdout surfaces and no secrets handled. That makes leakage possible mainly through unusual orchestration or manual transfer, not by default, and the blast radius appears limited because neither profile touches data classes.
conditions: IF an operator pastes sensitive content from B into A, A can exfiltrate it over the network.
IF B is later given file or clipboard access, shared-data leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in any text handed from B to A.
Keep B's file and clipboard surfaces disabled.
Route A through an egress allowlist.
Log and review any outbound requests from A.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on A's network traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes only broad network egress and no write surfaces; B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. With no overlapping mutable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF A is given filesystem or git write permissions outside the profile, overlap could emerge.
IF B is reconfigured with write access to a shared resource, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep B read-only as configured.
Do not grant A filesystem or git write access in the same workspace.
Separate any mutable resources by agent.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent, so B could treat A's generated text as input, but B is a customer-support profile with no documented action-taking authority or write surfaces. The pathway exists only if an operator or orchestrator forwards A's output into B without review.
conditions: IF A's generated text is forwarded to B as authoritative content, B may echo or rely on it.
IF an orchestrator skips human review between A and B, error propagation increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite sources before using A's claims.
Mark A output as draft-only.
Keep B from taking external actions based on A text.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. A touches no data classes and B lists no secrets handled, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to compare.
conditions: IF either profile later documents regulated data classes or residency constraints, compliance review should be revisited.
IF A or B is deployed under a regulated workload, additional policy checks may apply.
mitigations: Document data classes for both agents.
Record residency and retention policies before deployment.
Review any regulated-data workflow separately.
